intro_text.en: Unit 3 of Engineering Materials Science: the two branches of engineering metals, the carbon content that separates steel from cast iron, what each family of steel is ordered for, the four cast irons whose graphite shape decides their strength, and the copper and aluminium alloys that carry the current, save the weight and resist the sea. Every composition and strength quoted here is a handbook value, the designations are the ones used on an Indian drawing, and six solved numericals follow in section 3.6.
intro_text.gu: Engineering Materials Science નું Unit 3: ઇજનેરી ધાતુઓની બે શાખા, steel અને cast iron ને વહેંચતું carbon content, સ્ટીલનું દરેક કુટુંબ શેના માટે ઓર્ડર થાય, જેનો graphite આકાર તાકાત નક્કી કરે તે ચાર cast irons, અને current વહન કરતા, વજન બચાવતા તથી દરિયા સામે ટકતા copper તથી aluminium alloys. અહીંનું દરેક composition અને strength handbook નું મૂલ્ય છે, designations ભારતીય drawing પર વપરાતા છે, અને વિભાગ 3.6 માં છ ઉકેલેલા દાખલા છે.

title.en: 3.1 Classification of metals, and metals against non-metals
title.gu: 3.1 Metals નું વર્ગીકરણ, અને metals સામે non-metals

h.en: Two branches, and the carbon content that splits the first one
h.gu: બે શાખા, અને પહેલીને વહેંચતું carbon content

body.en:
Engineering metals are either ferrous - based on iron - or non-ferrous, based on some other metal. The ferrous branch splits at one number: 2.14 % carbon, the most that austenite can dissolve. Below it the material is steel, which can be rolled, forged and welded; above it the material is cast iron, which is poured into a mould and cannot be rolled because the eutectic at 4.3 % carbon makes it too brittle. Steel itself is described in two ways - by its carbon content (plain carbon steels) or by the element added to give it a property it did not have (alloy steels).

Why it is true. Everything in the ferrous branch follows from the iron-carbon diagram of Unit 2. Up to 2.14 % the carbon can hide inside austenite, so the metal can be deformed hot and becomes steel; beyond that the excess carbon has to appear as cementite at the grain boundaries, which is what makes white cast iron hard and unmachinable.

Ferrous શાખા એક જ આંકડા પર વહેંચાય છે: 2.14 % carbon, જેટલું austenite ઓગાળી શકે તે વધુમાં વધુ. તેની નીચે સામગ્રી steel છે, જે roll, forge અને weld કરી શકાય; તેની ઉપર cast iron છે, જે mould માં રેડાય છે અને roll થઈ શકતું નથી કારણ કે 4.3 % carbon પરનું eutectic તેને ખૂબ ભંગુર કરે છે. સ્ટીલને બે રીતે વર્ણવાય છે - તેના carbon content થી (plain carbon steels) અથવા જે element ઉમેરાય તે થી (alloy steels).

h.en: Metals and non-metals: one test settles it
h.gu: Metals અને non-metals: એક જ કસોટી નક્કી કરે

body.en:
A metal has free electrons that belong to the whole crystal instead of to a particular pair of atoms. Every other difference in the comparison below follows from that one: free electrons carry current and heat, reflect light (lustre), and allow layers of atoms to slide without breaking the bond, which is ductility. A non-metal holds its electrons in fixed bonds, so it insulates, looks dull and cracks instead of bending. Silicon and germanium sit between the two and are called metalloids.

PropertyMetalNon-metal
Electronsfree, shared by the crystalheld in fixed bonds
Conductionheat and current: copper 385 W/m Kinsulator; graphite and Si are exceptions
Deformationmalleable and ductilebrittle - it cracks
Lustreshiny, reflects lightdull
Melting pointusually high, 660 C to 3400 Clow (sulphur 115 C) or very high (diamond 3550 C)
Density2.7 to 19 g/cm3under 5 g/cm3
Oxidesbasic: Na2O, FeO, they react with acidacidic: CO2, SiO2, they react with alkali
sigma(copper) = 5.8e7 S/m sigma(glass) = 1e-12 S/m 5.8e7 / 1e-12 = 5.8e19 -> nineteen orders of magnitude one free electron per atom is the whole difference

Common mistake. Do not write 'metals are hard'. Lead is a metal and is softer than your thumb; diamond is a non-metal and scratches everything. Hardness is not the test - free electrons are.
body.gu:
ધાતુમાં free electrons હોય છે જે કોઈ એક જોડીના atoms ના નહીં પણ આખા crystal ના હોય. નીચેની સરખામણીનો બાકીનો દરેક ફરક એક જ વાત પરથી આવે: free electrons current અને ગરમી વહન કરે, પ્રકાશ પાછો ઝીલે (lustre), અને atoms ના સ્તરો bond તોડ્યા વગર સરકી શકે - એ જ ductility. Non-metal પોતાના electrons નિશ્ચિત bonds માં રાખે, તેથી તે અવાહક, ઝાંખું અને વળવાને બદલે તૂટે છે. Silicon અને germanium વચ્ચે બેસે છે અને તેમને metalloids કહે છે.

title.en: 3.2 Steels: plain carbon, alloy, and how they are ordered
title.gu: 3.2 Steels: plain carbon, alloy, અને તે કેવી રીતે ઓર્ડર થાય

h.en: Plain carbon steels: what carbon buys and what it costs
h.gu: Plain carbon steels: carbon શું આપે અને શું લે

body.en:
A plain carbon steel is iron with carbon and nothing else that matters - manganese up to 0.8 % for deoxidation and sulphur and phosphorus kept low. Everything about it follows from the volume fraction of pearlite, and that follows from the carbon content. More carbon means more cementite, so the steel gets stronger and harder and less ductile and less weldable. The strength roughly doubles between 0.1 % and 1.2 % carbon while the elongation falls from 30 % to 5 %, which is why the useful engineering steels sit between 0.2 % and 0.5 %.

h.en: Alloy steels, stainless steel and how a designation is read
h.gu: Alloy steels, stainless steel અને designation કેવી રીતે વાંચવું

body.en:
Carbon alone cannot give a thick section that hardens all the way through, nor a surface that resists rust, nor a steel that stays tough at 500 C. An alloy steel adds one or more elements to buy exactly those properties: chromium above 12 % forms a passive oxide film (stainless), nickel raises toughness and makes the austenite stable at room temperature (18/8), molybdenum raises hardenability and high-temperature strength, vanadium and tungsten keep the hardness at red heat (tool steels), and small amounts of niobium or titanium give the fine-grain high-strength low-alloy steels used in pipelines.

SS 30418 Cr, 8 Ni, 0.08 Ccorrosion resistance, weldablekitchen, dairy, architecture

Common mistake. Stainless steel is not 'steel that cannot rust'. It is steel whose chromium makes a self-healing oxide skin. Scratch it in chloride water, or heat it to 600 C and let chromium carbide form at the grain boundaries, and it corrodes like any steel.

ફક્ત carbon થી જાડો ભાગ આખો harden થાય, સપાટી કાટ સામે ટકે, કે 500 C પર toughness જળવાય તે શક્ય નથી. Alloy steel એ એક કે વધુ element ઉમેરીને બરાબર એ ગુણધર્મ ખરીદે છે: 12 % થી ઉપર chromium passive oxide પડ બનાવે (stainless), nickel toughness વધારે અને austenite ને room temperature પર ટકાવે (18/8), molybdenum hardenability અને ઊંચા temperature ની તાકાત વધારે, vanadium અને tungsten લાલ ગરમીમાં પણ hardness રાખે (tool steels), અને થોડું niobium કે titanium pipeline માં વપરાતું fine-grain high-strength low-alloy સ્ટીલ આપે.

title.en: 3.3 Cast irons: the shape of the graphite decides everything
title.gu: 3.3 Cast irons: graphite નો આકાર બધું નક્કી કરે

h.en: Four cast irons and what each one is good at
h.gu: ચાર cast irons અને દરેક શેમાં સારું છે

body.en:
A cast iron holds 2.5 to 4 % carbon and 1 to 3 % silicon, and that is far more carbon than iron can keep in solution - so the carbon comes out of the melt as either graphite or cementite. Which one it becomes, and what shape the graphite takes, decides the properties completely. Grey iron cools slowly in a sand mould and its graphite forms flakes: cheap, easy to cast, an excellent damper, but weak in tension because every flake is a crack. White iron cools fast or is low in silicon, keeps its carbon as cementite, and is so hard it can only be ground. Malleable iron is white iron that has been annealed until the cementite breaks down into rosettes of temper carbon, and ductile (SG) iron is grey iron whose graphite was made to grow as nodules by adding a little magnesium.

Cast ironC %GraphiteUTS (MPa)ElongationUsed for
Grey3.2 - 3.6flakes150 - 3000.5 %machine beds, housings, covers

carbon equivalent: CE = %C + (%Si + %P)/3 grey iron C 3.4, Si 2.1, P 0.3: CE = 3.4 + 2.4/3 = 4.20 (just below eutectic) ductile iron C 3.6, Si 2.4: CE = 3.6 + 2.4/3 = 4.40 (just above) CE near 4.3 gives the best fluidity and the easiest casting

Why it is true. Silicon does the same job as carbon: it is a graphitiser, pushing the carbon out of solution. That is why the carbon equivalent adds a third of the silicon - 1 % of silicon behaves like 0.33 % of carbon. Raise it too far and graphite forms before the metal freezes (kish graphite), which floats and leaves a rough surface.

h.en: Cast iron against steel, and why a machine bed is cast iron
h.gu: Cast iron સામે steel, અને machine bed cast iron કેમ હોય

body.en:
The difference between the two is not just composition. A cast iron contains graphite flakes, and a flake is a free surface: it cannot carry tensile stress, it absorbs vibration as the two faces rub, and it holds oil so the surface stays lubricated. So cast iron is weak in tension, roughly three to four times stronger in compression, superb at damping and cheap to make into a complicated shape. Steel has no graphite, so it is equally strong in tension and compression, can be forged and welded, and takes shock without cracking.

Pure copper conducts better than any metal except silver - 385 W/(m K) and 100 % of the international annealed copper standard - but it is soft, 220 MPa, and expensive. Adding a second metal raises its strength and hardness and destroys part of that conductivity, because the dissolved atoms scatter the free electrons. With zinc it becomes brass: 70/30 is soft and ductile, ideal for deep drawing and radiator fins, while 60/40 is stronger and is extruded into rod for screws. With tin it becomes bronze, harder and very wear resistant, the classic bearing and bell metal. Adding both gives gunmetal, which resists sea water and is cast into pump bodies and valve chests.

Why it is true. A pure metal conducts well because its electrons see a perfectly regular lattice. title.en: 3.5 Aluminium: wrought alloys, cast alloys and tempers
title.gu: 3.5 Aluminium: wrought alloys, cast alloys અને tempers

h.en: The eight series and what the number tells you
h.gu: આઠ series અને આંકડો શું કહે છે

body.en:
Aluminium is light - 2.70 g/cm3, a third of steel - and it protects itself with a thin oxide film, so it does not rust. Pure aluminium is soft, only 110 MPa, so almost everything used is an alloy. The wrought alloys are numbered by their main alloying element, and the first digit says which: series 1 (1050) is 99 % pure, series 2 (2024) is copper, strong but not weldable, which is why an aircraft skin is riveted, series 3 (3003) is manganese for kitchen foil and utensils, series 4 (4043) is silicon for brazing sheet, series 5 (5052) is magnesium for marine plate because it is the best of them at welding and at sea water, series 6 (6061) is magnesium plus silicon and is the extrusion alloy of window frames, ladders and structures, series 7 (7075) is zinc, the strongest at 570 MPa, used for an aircraft wing, and series 8 (8006) is everything else.

Why it is true. The T tempers work by precipitation. The alloy is heated to dissolve the alloying elements, quenched to trap them in a supersaturated solution, then held warm so that fine particles precipitate and block dislocations. Nothing is added and nothing is removed - the strength comes entirely from the heat treatment, which is why the temper letter has to be written with the alloy number.

h.en: Cast alloys, and choosing aluminium against steel
h.gu: Cast alloys, અને steel સામે aluminium પસંદ કરવું

body.en:
Casting alloys are numbered differently, by a three-digit system and a decimal, because a casting cannot be rolled to close its porosity. The workhorse is LM6, an Al-12 % Si alloy: silicon lowers the melting point and makes the metal fluid, so it fills a mould and casts almost without shrinkage, and the result is light, corrosion-resistant and dimensionally stable - pistons, manifolds and pump bodies. A356 with a T6 temper reaches 260 MPa and is used for wheels and gearbox housings. Cast alloys reach about 300 MPa against 600 for the best wrought alloys, so anything highly stressed is forged rather than cast.

h.en: Density of a 70/30 brass from the rule of mixtures
h.gu: Rule of mixtures થી 70/30 brass ની density

body.en:
Question (7 marks)

A 70/30 brass is made by weight from copper (8.96 g/cm3) and zinc (7.14 g/cm3). Estimate its density by adding volumes, compare it with the measured 8.53 g/cm3 and say why the estimate is low.

Step 1 - the volume of 100 g of alloy

take 100 g of brass: 70 g copper and 30 g zinc V(Cu) = 70/8.96 = 7.8125 cm3 V(Zn) = 30/7.14 = 4.2017 cm3 V(total) = 12.0142 cm3

Step 2 - the density

rho = m/V = 100/12.0142 = 8.32 g/cm3 in the rule form: 1/rho = 0.70/8.96 + 0.30/7.14 = 0.12014

Step 3 - compare and explain

measured 8.53 g/cm3, estimated 8.32 g/cm3 error = (8.32 - 8.53)/8.53 x 100 = -2.5 %
rho = 8.32 g/cm3 against 8.53 measured: 2.5 % low

The rule of mixtures assumes the atoms simply add their volumes, but a zinc atom is smaller than a copper atom and fits into the lattice without pushing it apart, so the real alloy is denser than the sum of its parts. The same assumption is why the rule is only used for an estimate, never for a purchase specification.

Check your answer. A rough check: the answer must lie between 7.14 and 8.96, and nearer to copper because there is more copper. 8.32 satisfies both.
body.gu:
પ્રશ્ન (7 marks)

70/30 brass વજન પ્રમાણે copper (8.96 g/cm3) અને zinc (7.14 g/cm3) થી બને છે. Volume ઉમેરીને તેની density નો અંદાજ કાઢો, માપેલા 8.53 g/cm3 સાથે સરખાવો અને અંદાજ ઓછો કેમ આવે તે કહો.

પગલું 1 - 100 g alloy નું volume

take 100 g of brass: 70 g copper and 30 g zinc V(Cu) = 70/8.96 = 7.8125 cm3 V(Zn) = 30/7.14 = 4.2017 cm3 V(total) = 12.0142 cm3

પગલું 2 - density

rho = m/V = 100/12.0142 = 8.32 g/cm3 in the rule form: 1/rho = 0.70/8.96 + 0.30/7.14 = 0.12014

પગલું 3 - સરખાવો અને સમજાવો

measured 8.53 g/cm3, estimated 8.32 g/cm3 error = (8.32 - 8.53)/8.53 x 100 = -2.5 %
rho = 8.32 g/cm3 against 8.53 measured: 2.5 % low

Rule of mixtures ધારે છે કે atoms ફક્ત પોતાનું volume ઉમેરે, પણ zinc atom copper atom કરતાં નાનો હોય તેથી lattice ને ધકેલ્યા વગર અંદર બેસે, અને સાચો alloy તેના ભાગોના સરવાળા કરતાં ઘનતાવાળો નીકળે. એ જ કારણે આ નિયમ ફક્ત અંદાજ માટે વપરાય, ખરીદીના specification માટે નહીં.

જવાબ ચકાસો. ઝડપી ચકાસણી: જવાબ 7.14 અને 8.96 વચ્ચે અને copper ની નજીક હોવો જોઈએ કારણ કે copper વધુ છે. 8.32 બંને શરત પૂરી કરે છે.

body.en:
Question (7 marks)

A foundry needs 250 kg of sound 70/30 brass castings. Melting loss is 3 % of the charge. Copper costs Rs 820 per kg and zinc Rs 280 per kg. Find the charge mass and the metal cost of the heat.

Step 1 - the charge mass

3 % is lost, so 97 % of the charge becomes casting 0.97 x charge = 250 kg charge = 250/0.97 = 257.7 kg

Step 2 - cost of one kilogram of charge

70 % copper: 0.70 x 820 = Rs 574.00 30 % zinc: 0.30 x 280 = Rs 84.00 cost per kg = Rs 658.00

Step 3 - the cost of the heat

cost = 257.7 x 658 = Rs 1,69,587 per kilogram of good casting: 169587/250 = Rs 678.3
charge 257.7 kg, Rs 1,69,587 for the heat, Rs 678 per kg of casting

The melting loss is what makes the casting cost more than the metal in it: 3 % of the charge is lost, so about Rs 20 per kilogram of casting is paid for metal that went up the flue or into the slag. That is why a foundry weighs its charge and its returns carefully.

Common mistake. Do not add 3 % to 250 kg. The loss is taken from the charge, so the charge is larger than the casting by 250/0.97, not 250 x 1.03.
body.gu:
પ્રશ્ન (7 marks)

એક ફાઉન્ડ્રીને 250 kg સાચા 70/30 brass castings જોઈએ. Melting loss charge ના 3 % છે. Copper Rs 820 પ્રતિ kg અને zinc Rs 280 પ્રતિ kg. Charge નું દળ અને heat નો metal ખર્ચ શોધો.

પગલું 1 - charge નું દળ

3 % is lost, so 97 % of the charge becomes casting 0.97 x charge = 250 kg charge = 250/0.97 = 257.7 kg

પગલું 2 - એક kg charge નો ખર્ચ

70 % copper: 0.70 x 820 = Rs 574.00 30 % zinc: 0.30 x 280 = Rs 84.00 cost per kg = Rs 658.00

પગલું 3 - heat નો ખર્ચ

cost = 257.7 x 658 = Rs 1,69,587 per kilogram of good casting: 169587/250 = Rs 678.3
charge 257.7 kg, Rs 1,69,587 for the heat, Rs 678 per kg of casting

Melting loss એ જ casting ને તેમાંના metal કરતાં મોંઘું બનાવે: charge ના 3 % જાય છે, તેથી casting ના પ્રતિ kg લગભગ Rs 20 એવી ધાતુના મળે જે ચીમનીમાં કે slag માં ગઈ. તેથી ફાઉન્ડ્રી પોતાનું charge અને returns કાળજીથી તોલે છે.

સામાન્ય ભૂલ. 250 kg માં 3 % ઉમેરશો નહીં. Loss charge માંથી જાય છે, તેથી charge casting કરતાં 250/0.97 જેટલું મોટું હોય, 250 x 1.03 નહીં.

h.en: Carbon equivalent of two cast irons
h.gu: બે cast irons નું carbon equivalent

body.en:
Question (6 marks)

A grey iron contains 3.4 % C, 2.1 % Si and 0.3 % P; a ductile iron contains 3.6 % C, 2.4 % Si and 0.05 % P. Find the carbon equivalent of each and say what it means for casting.

Step 1 - the formula

CE = %C + (%Si + %P)/3 silicon graphitises a third as strongly as carbon, hence the divisor 3

Step 2 - the grey iron

CE = 3.4 + (2.1 + 0.3)/3 = 3.4 + 0.80 = 4.20

Step 3 - the ductile iron

CE = 3.6 + (2.4 + 0.05)/3 = 3.6 + 0.817 = 4.42
grey iron CE = 4.20, ductile iron CE = 4.42, the eutectic is 4.3

Both are close to the eutectic value of 4.3, which is what a foundry wants: a metal that freezes in a narrow range, feeds itself, and casts without shrinkage cavities. The grey iron at 4.20 is slightly hypoeutectic and will show a little primary austenite; the ductile iron at 4.42 is slightly hypereutectic, and it is the magnesium addition, not the carbon, that makes its graphite nodular.

Check your answer. CE must not be far above 4.3 in a thin section, or kish graphite forms and the casting surface becomes rough and weak.
body.gu:
પ્રશ્ન (6 marks)

એક grey iron માં 3.4 % C, 2.1 % Si અને 0.3 % P છે; એક ductile iron માં 3.6 % C, 2.4 % Si અને 0.05 % P છે. દરેકનું carbon equivalent શોધો અને casting માટે તેનો અર્થ કહો.

પગલું 1 - સૂત્ર

CE = %C + (%Si + %P)/3 silicon graphitises a third as strongly as carbon, hence the divisor 3

પગલું 2 - grey iron

CE = 3.4 + (2.1 + 0.3)/3 = 3.4 + 0.80 = 4.20

પગલું 3 - ductile iron

CE = 3.6 + (2.4 + 0.05)/3 = 3.6 + 0.817 = 4.42
grey iron CE = 4.20, ductile iron CE = 4.42, the eutectic is 4.3

બંને eutectic મૂલ્ય 4.3 ની નજીક છે, જે ફાઉન્ડ્રીને જોઈએ: એવી ધાતુ જે નાની range માં થીજે, પોતાને feed કરે અને shrinkage છિદ્રો વગર cast થાય. 4.20 વાળું grey iron થોડું hypoeutectic છે અને થોડું primary austenite દેખાશે; 4.42 વાળું ductile iron થોડું hypereutectic છે, અને તેનું graphite nodular magnesium ઉમેરવાથી થાય છે, carbon થી નહીં.

જવાબ ચકાસો. પાતળા ભાગમાં CE 4.3 થી ઘણું ઉપર ન જોઈએ, નહીં તો kish graphite બને અને casting ની સપાટી ખરબચડી તથી નબળી થાય.

h.en: Replacing a steel bracket with aluminium
h.gu: Steel bracket ને aluminium થી બદલવું

body.en:
Question (6 marks)

A bracket has a volume of 260 cm3 and is made of steel of density 7.85 g/cm3. Find its mass, the mass if it is made of aluminium alloy of density 2.70 g/cm3, and the percentage saved. The steel has UTS 450 MPa and the aluminium alloy 310 MPa - comment on whether the swap is safe at the same dimensions.

Step 1 - the two masses

m(steel) = rho V = 7.85 x 260 = 2041 g = 2.04 kg m(aluminium) = 2.70 x 260 = 702 g = 0.70 kg

Step 2 - the saving

saving = 2.041 - 0.702 = 1.339 kg percentage = 1.339/2.041 x 100 = 65.6 %

Step 3 - is it safe at the same size?

section area is unchanged, so the load capacity falls in the ratio of the strengths 310/450 = 0.69 - the aluminium part carries 69 % of the load specific strength: steel 450/7.85 = 57, aluminium 310/2.70 = 115 kN m/kg so the swap is safe only if the part was over-designed by 45 % or can be thickened
2.04 kg -> 0.70 kg, 65.6 % lighter, but 31 % weaker at the same section

This is the standard trap of a material substitution question. Weight falls by two thirds, but strength falls by a third, and stiffness falls by two thirds as well because the modulus of aluminium is 70 GPa against 200 GPa for steel. A part that is stiffness-limited must be redesigned, not just swapped.

Check your answer. Check the units: 260 cm3 x 7.85 g/cm3 gives grams, so divide by 1000 for kilograms.
body.gu:
પ્રશ્ન (6 marks)

એક bracket નું volume 260 cm3 છે અને તે 7.85 g/cm3 density ના સ્ટીલનું બનેલું છે. તેનું દળ, 2.70 g/cm3 density ના aluminium alloy નું બન્યું હોય તો દળ, અને થતી ટકાવારી બચત શોધો. સ્ટીલનું UTS 450 MPa અને aluminium alloy નું 310 MPa છે - સરખા માપ પર આ બદલી સલામત છે કે નહીં તે કહો.

પગલું 1 - બે દળ

m(steel) = rho V = 7.85 x 260 = 2041 g = 2.04 kg m(aluminium) = 2.70 x 260 = 702 g = 0.70 kg

પગલું 2 - બચત

saving = 2.041 - 0.702 = 1.339 kg percentage = 1.339/2.041 x 100 = 65.6 %

પગલું 3 - સરખા માપ પર સલામત છે?

section area is unchanged, so the load capacity falls in the ratio of the strengths 310/450 = 0.69 - the aluminium part carries 69 % of the load specific strength: steel 450/7.85 = 57, aluminium 310/2.70 = 115 kN m/kg so the swap is safe only if the part was over-designed by 45 % or can be thickened
2.04 kg -> 0.70 kg, 65.6 % lighter, but 31 % weaker at the same section

સામગ્રી બદલવાના પ્રશ્નની આ પ્રમાણભૂત ભૂલ છે. વજન બે-તૃતીયાંશ ઘટે, પણ તાકાત એક-તૃતીયાંશ ઘટે, અને stiffness પણ બે-તૃતીયાંશ ઘટે કારણ કે aluminium નો modulus 70 GPa છે જ્યારે સ્ટીલનો 200 GPa. Stiffness-મર્યાદિત ભાગ ફરી design કરવો પડે, ફક્ત બદલી નાખવાથી ન થાય.

જવાબ ચકાસો. એકમ ચકાસો: 260 cm3 x 7.85 g/cm3 ગ્રામ આપે, તેથી kg માટે 1000 વડે ભાગો.

h.en: Copper or brass for a wire

body.en:
Question (7 marks)

A 30 m run of 2.5 mm2 wire is to carry 16 A. Compare the resistance and the power lost if the wire is copper (1.72e-8 ohm m) and if it is brass (6.4e-8 ohm m), and say which one a switchboard uses.

Step 1 - the resistance of each

R = rho L/A, A = 2.5 mm2 = 2.5e-6 m2, L = 30 m R(Cu) = 1.72e-8 x 30/2.5e-6 = 0.2064 ohm R(brass) = 6.40e-8 x 30/2.5e-6 = 0.7680 ohm

Step 2 - the power lost at 16 A

P = I^2 R P(Cu) = 16^2 x 0.2064 = 52.8 W P(brass) = 16^2 x 0.7680 = 196.6 W

Step 3 - compare

resistance ratio = 6.4/1.72 = 3.72 extra loss = 196.6 - 52.8 = 143.8 W in 30 m of wire over a 10 hour day: 1.44 kWh wasted per run
0.206 ohm against 0.768 ohm; 52.8 W against 196.6 W; copper by a factor of 3.7

A switchboard uses copper, or aluminium where the weight matters more than the loss, and never brass. Brass is for a terminal stud or a plug pin, where its strength and its machinability matter and the current path is a few millimetres long.

Common mistake. Area in mm2 must be converted to m2 before it goes into R = rho L/A, otherwise the answer is a million times too small.
body.gu:
પ્રશ્ન (7 marks)

2.5 mm2 ની 30 m લાંબી wire 16 A વહન કરે છે. Wire copper (1.72e-8 ohm m) હોય અને brass (6.4e-8 ohm m) હોય તો resistance અને ગુમાવાતી power સરખાવો, અને switchboard કઈ વાપરે તે કહો.

પગલું 1 - દરેકનું resistance

R = rho L/A, A = 2.5 mm2 = 2.5e-6 m2, L = 30 m R(Cu) = 1.72e-8 x 30/2.5e-6 = 0.2064 ohm R(brass) = 6.40e-8 x 30/2.5e-6 = 0.7680 ohm

પગલું 2 - 16 A પર ગુમાવાતી power

P = I^2 R P(Cu) = 16^2 x 0.2064 = 52.8 W P(brass) = 16^2 x 0.7680 = 196.6 W

પગલું 3 - સરખામણી

resistance ratio = 6.4/1.72 = 3.72 extra loss = 196.6 - 52.8 = 143.8 W in 30 m of wire over a 10 hour day: 1.44 kWh wasted per run
0.206 ohm against 0.768 ohm; 52.8 W against 196.6 W; copper by a factor of 3.7

Switchboard copper વાપરે, અથવા જ્યાં ગુમાવેલા power કરતાં વજન વધુ મહત્વનું હોય ત્યાં aluminium, અને brass કદી નહીં. Brass terminal stud કે plug pin માટે છે, જ્યાં તેની તાકાત અને machining ઉપયોગી છે અને current નો રસ્તો થોડા મિલીમીટરનો છે.

સામાન્ય ભૂલ. R = rho L/A માં નાખતાં પહેલાં mm2 નું area m2 માં ફેરવવું પડે, નહીં તો જવાબ દસ લાખ ગણો નાનો આવે.

h.en: From weight per cent to atomic per cent

body.en:
Question (6 marks)

A 70/30 brass and a gunmetal of composition Cu 88, Sn 10, Zn 2 are given by weight. Convert both to atomic per cent (Cu 63.55, Zn 65.38, Sn 118.71) and say why a metallurgist prefers the atomic figure.

Step 1 - moles in 100 g of brass

n(Cu) = 70/63.55 = 1.1015 mol n(Zn) = 30/65.38 = 0.4589 mol total = 1.5604 mol

Step 2 - atomic per cent of the brass

Cu = 1.1015/1.5604 x 100 = 70.6 at % Zn = 0.4589/1.5604 x 100 = 29.4 at %

Step 3 - the gunmetal

n(Cu) = 88/63.55 = 1.3847, n(Sn) = 10/118.71 = 0.0842, n(Zn) = 2/65.38 = 0.0306 total = 1.4995 mol Cu 92.3 at %, Sn 5.6 at %, Zn 2.0 at %
brass 70.6 / 29.4 at %, gunmetal 92.3 / 5.6 / 2.0 at %

A phase diagram, a lattice parameter and a density calculation all count atoms, not grams, so the atomic per cent is the composition you need for any structural argument. A datasheet gives weight per cent because that is what the foundry weighs out.

Check your answer. The atomic percentages must still add to 100: 70.6 + 29.4 = 100.0 and 92.3 + 5.6 + 2.0 = 99.9, which is rounding.
body.gu:
પ્રશ્ન (6 marks)

70/30 brass અને Cu 88, Sn 10, Zn 2 ના gunmetal વજન પ્રમાણે આપેલા છે. બંનેને atomic ટકામાં ફેરવો (Cu 63.55, Zn 65.38, Sn 118.71) અને metallurgist atomic આંકડો કેમ પસંદ કરે તે કહો.

પગલું 1 - 100 g brass માં moles

n(Cu) = 70/63.55 = 1.1015 mol n(Zn) = 30/65.38 = 0.4589 mol total = 1.5604 mol

પગલું 2 - brass ના atomic ટકા

Cu = 1.1015/1.5604 x 100 = 70.6 at % Zn = 0.4589/1.5604 x 100 = 29.4 at %

પગલું 3 - gunmetal

n(Cu) = 88/63.55 = 1.3847, n(Sn) = 10/118.71 = 0.0842, n(Zn) = 2/65.38 = 0.0306 total = 1.4995 mol Cu 92.3 at %, Sn 5.6 at %, Zn 2.0 at %
brass 70.6 / 29.4 at %, gunmetal 92.3 / 5.6 / 2.0 at %

Phase diagram, lattice parameter અને density ની ગણતરી બધું atoms ગણે, ગ્રામ નહીં, તેથી કોઈ પણ રચનાની દલીલ માટે atomic ટકા જોઈએ. Datasheet વજનના ટકા આપે કારણ કે ફાઉન્ડ્રી તોલે છે તે વજન.

જવાબ ચકાસો. Atomic ટકાનો સરવાળો પણ 100 થવો જોઈએ: 70.6 + 29.4 = 100.0 અને 92.3 + 5.6 + 2.0 = 99.9, જે rounding છે.

caption.en: Ferrous means iron-based: steel up to 2.14 % carbon and cast iron above it, split by the carbon content and the graphite shape. Non-ferrous means everything else, one base metal plus what is added to it.
caption.gu: Ferrous એટલે iron પર આધારિત: 2.14 % carbon સુધી steel અને તેની ઉપર cast iron, જે carbon content તથી graphite ના આકાર પ્રમાણે વહેંચાય. Non-ferrous એટલે બાકીનું બધું, એક base metal અને તેમાં ઉમેરેલું.

caption.en: Raising carbon from 0.1 % to 1.2 % nearly doubles the tensile strength and cuts the elongation from 30 % to 5 %; the best combination is in the middle.
caption.gu: Carbon 0.1 % થી 1.2 % કરો તો tensile strength લગભગ બમણી થાય અને elongation 30 % થી 5 % થાય; સૌથી સારું સંયોજન વચ્ચે મળે છે.

caption.en: All four cast irons hold more than 2 % carbon; what changes is the shape the carbon takes - flakes, cementite, temper carbon or nodules - and that shape decides the strength.
caption.gu: ચારેય cast irons માં 2 % થી વધુ carbon હોય છે; બદલાય છે carbon જે આકાર લે છે - flakes, cementite, temper carbon કે nodules - અને એ આકાર તાકાત નક્કી કરે છે.

caption.en: Zinc raises the strength of copper and destroys its conductivity at the same time, so electrical work uses copper and bearing work uses bronze.
caption.gu: Zinc copper ની તાકાત વધારે અને તે જ વખતે વાહકતા નષ્ટ કરે, તેથી electrical કામમાં copper અને bearing ના કામમાં bronze વપરાય.

caption.en: A steel is ordered by its designation, and the number in the middle is the carbon in hundredths of a per cent.
caption.gu: સ્ટીલ તેના designation થી ઓર્ડર થાય, અને વચ્ચેનો આંકડો ટકાના સોમાં ભાગમાં carbon છે.

caption.en: The aluminium series number says which element is the main alloying addition; a series 7 zinc alloy reaches 570 MPa, more than twice what plain carbon steel gives at the same weight.
caption.gu: Series નો આંકડો કહે છે કે મુખ્ય alloying ઉમેરો કયો છે; series 7 ના zinc alloys 570 MPa સુધી પહોંચે, જે સરખા વજનના plain carbon steel કરતાં બમણાથી વધુ છે.

caption.en: Metals and non-metals are separated by one property - whether the outer electrons are free - and every other difference in the table follows from it.
caption.gu: Metals અને non-metals એક જ ગુણધર્મથી અલગ પડે - outer electrons મુક્ત છે કે નહીં - અને કોષ્ટકનો બાકીનો દરેક ફરક એમાંથી આવે છે.

terms.en: How every alloy composition in a datasheet is written.
terms.gu: Datasheet માં દરેક alloy composition આમ જ લખાય છે.

terms.en: A is the atomic mass; needed whenever atoms, not grams, do the work.
terms.gu: A એ atomic mass; જ્યાં atoms કામ કરે ત્યાં grams નહીં, આ જોઈએ.

terms.en: Volume-additive estimate; 2 to 3 % low when the atoms pack better than ideal.
terms.gu: Volume-ઉમેરાતો અંદાજ; atoms આદર્શ કરતાં સારા ગોઠવાય તો 2-3 % ઓછો આવે.

name.en: Carbon equivalent of a cast iron

terms.en: Silicon graphitises a third as strongly as carbon; CE near 4.3 casts best.
terms.gu: Silicon, carbon ના ત્રીજા ભાગ જેટલું graphitise કરે; CE 4.3 ની આસપાસ સૌથી સારું cast થાય.

terms.en: MPa/(g/cm3) is the same number as kN m/kg; the fair comparison for weight.
terms.gu: MPa/(g/cm3) એ kN m/kg જ છે; વજન માટેની ન્યાયી સરખામણી.

terms.en: 5.8e7 S/m is annealed copper; brass 70/30 is 28 % of it.
terms.gu: 5.8e7 S/m એ annealed copper છે; brass 70/30 તેના 28 % જેટલું.

terms.en: Steel 7.85, cast iron 7.2, copper 8.96, aluminium 2.70 g/cm3.
terms.gu: આંકડા: steel 7.85, cast iron 7.2, copper 8.96, aluminium 2.70 g/cm3.

terms.en: Steel ends at 2.14 % C; cast iron runs from there to 6.67 %.
terms.gu: Steel 2.14 % C પર પૂરું થાય; cast iron ત્યાંથી 6.67 % સુધી.

items.f: Cr >= 12 % for a continuous passive film

terms.en: 18/8 means 18 % Cr and 8 % Ni: austenitic and non-magnetic.
terms.gu: 18/8 એટલે 18 % Cr અને 8 % Ni: austenitic અને non-magnetic.

items.f: C 45 = 0.45 % C;  EN8 is the same steel under the old BS name

terms.en: The number is the carbon in hundredths of a per cent.
terms.gu: આંકડો એટલે ટકાના સોમાં ભાગમાં carbon.

items.f: flake = grey,  nodule = ductile,  rosette = malleable,  none = white

terms.en: The shape, not the carbon content, sets the strength.
terms.gu: તાકાત carbon content નહીં, આકાર નક્કી કરે.

items.f: sigma(compression) = 3 to 4 x sigma(tension) for grey iron

terms.en: A flake is a crack, so it opens in tension and closes in compression.
terms.gu: Flake એ તિરાડ છે, તેથી tension માં ખૂલે અને compression માં બંધ થાય.

items.f: damping of grey iron = 5 to 10 x that of steel

terms.en: The reason a lathe bed and a surface plate are cast iron.
terms.gu: Lathe bed અને surface plate cast iron કેમ હોય તેનું કારણ.

items.f: series 1 = 99 % Al; 2 = Cu; 3 = Mn; 4 = Si; 5 = Mg; 6 = Mg+Si; 7 = Zn; 8 = other

terms.en: The number says the main alloying element of a wrought alloy.
terms.gu: આંકડો wrought alloy નું મુખ્ય alloying element કહે છે.

items.f: temper: O = annealed, H = strain hardened, T = solution treated + aged, F = as fabricated

terms.en: Always written with the alloy: 6061-T6, not 6061.
terms.gu: હંમેશા alloy સાથે લખાય: 6061-T6, ફક્ત 6061 નહીં.

terms.en: Every dissolved atom scatters electrons, so strength costs conductivity.
terms.gu: દરેક ઓગળેલો atom electrons ને અથડાવે, તેથી તાકાત વાહકતાનો ભોગ લે.

q.en: What separates steel from cast iron?
q.gu: Steel અને cast iron ને શું વહેંચે છે?

a.en: The carbon content. Up to 2.14 % it is steel, above it cast iron, and 2.14 % is the most carbon austenite can dissolve.
a.gu: Carbon content. 2.14 % સુધી steel, ઉપર cast iron, અને 2.14 % એ austenite ઓગાળી શકે તે વધુમાં વધુ carbon.

q.en: Give three differences between a metal and a non-metal.
q.gu: Metal અને non-metal વચ્ચે ત્રણ ફરક આપો.

a.en: A metal conducts heat and current, is malleable and ductile, and has lustre; a non-metal insulates, is brittle, and is dull. All three come from free electrons.
a.gu: Metal ગરમી અને current વહન કરે, malleable તથી ductile છે, અને lustre ધરાવે; non-metal અવાહક, ભંગુર અને ઝાંખું છે. ત્રણેય free electrons થી આવે.

q.en: Why is silicon called a metalloid?
q.gu: Silicon ને metalloid કેમ કહે છે?

a.en: It looks like a metal - shiny and grey - but it is brittle and is a semiconductor, not a conductor.
a.gu: તે ધાતુ જેવું દેખાય - ચળકતું અને ભૂખરું - પણ તે ભંગુર છે અને conductor નહીં, semiconductor છે.

q.en: Why does strength rise with carbon and ductility fall?
q.gu: Carbon વધતાં તાકાત કેમ વધે અને ductility કેમ ઘટે?

a.en: More carbon means more cementite in the pearlite, and cementite is hard and brittle; the ferrite that used to deform is replaced by it.
a.gu: વધુ carbon એટલે pearlite માં વધુ cementite, અને cementite સખત તથી ભંગુર છે; જે ferrite deform થતું હતું તેની જગ્યાએ તે આવે છે.

q.en: What does EN19 steel contain and where is it used?
q.gu: EN19 સ્ટીલમાં શું છે અને ક્યાં વપરાય?

a.en: 0.4 % carbon with about 1 % chromium and 0.25 % molybdenum, so it hardens right through a thick section: gears, crankshafts and axles.
a.gu: 0.4 % carbon સાથે લગભગ 1 % chromium અને 0.25 % molybdenum, તેથી જાડો ભાગ પણ આખો harden થાય: gears, crankshafts અને axles.

q.en: Why is stainless steel called stainless?
q.gu: Stainless steel ને stainless કેમ કહે છે?

a.en: Because its chromium forms a thin passive oxide film that heals itself in air. Without oxygen, or in chloride water, it is not stainless at all.
a.gu: કારણ કે તેનું chromium પાતળું passive oxide પડ બનાવે જે હવામાં પોતાની જાતે સંધાય. Oxygen ન હોય કે chloride વાળા પાણીમાં તે stainless જ નથી.

q.en: Why is grey cast iron good for a lathe bed?
q.gu: Lathe bed માટે grey cast iron કેમ સારું છે?

a.en: It is loaded in compression, where it is strong; the graphite damps vibration so the finish stays accurate; and the complicated shape is cast, not machined.
a.gu: તેના પર compression નો ભાર હોય જ્યાં તે મજબૂત છે; graphite vibration શોષે તેથી finish ચોક્કસ રહે; અને ગૂંચવાડાભરી આકૃતિ cast થાય, machined નહીં.

q.en: What is the difference between brass and bronze?
q.gu: Brass અને bronze માં શું ફરક છે?

a.en: Brass is copper with zinc, and bronze is copper with tin; brass is more ductile and cheaper, bronze is harder and better under wear.
a.gu: Brass એ copper સાથે zinc, અને bronze એ copper સાથે tin; brass વધુ ductile અને સસ્તું, bronze વધુ સખત અને wear માં સારું.

q.en: Why does adding zinc to copper reduce its conductivity?
q.gu: Copper માં zinc ઉમેરતાં વાહકતા કેમ ઘટે છે?

a.en: The zinc atoms are a different size, so they strain the lattice and scatter the conduction electrons; scattering is resistance.
a.gu: Zinc atoms જુદા માપના હોય તેથી lattice તણાય અને conduction electrons અથડાય; અથડામણ એ resistance છે.

a.en: The main alloying addition is magnesium plus silicon in a series 6 alloy; the other digits identify the particular composition.
a.gu: series 6 alloy માં મુખ્ય alloying ઉમેરો magnesium અને silicon છે; બાકીના અંક ચોક્કસ composition ઓળખે છે.

q.en: What does the T6 temper mean?

a.en: Solution heat treated, quenched and then artificially aged, so that fine precipitates block dislocations and raise the strength.
a.gu: Solution heat treatment, quench અને પછી artificial ageing, જેથી નાના precipitates dislocation રોકે અને તાકાત વધારે.

q.en: Why can aluminium not simply replace steel part for part?
q.gu: Aluminium સ્ટીલની જગ્યાએ ભાગ-બદલ ભાગ કેમ ન લઈ શકે?

a.en: It is a third of the density but also a third of the modulus, so a part of the same size deflects three times as much; a strength-limited part must be compared on specific strength.
a.gu: તેની density ત્રીજા ભાગની છે પણ modulus પણ ત્રીજા ભાગનો, તેથી સરખા માપનો ભાગ ત્રણ ગણો વળે; તાકાત-મર્યાદિત ભાગ specific strength પર સરખાવવો પડે.

q.en: A 70/30 brass is made by weight from copper (8.96 g/cm3) and zinc (7.14 g/cm3). Estimate its density by adding volumes, compare it with the measured 8.53 g/cm3 and say why the estimate is low.
q.gu: 70/30 brass વજન પ્રમાણે copper (8.96 g/cm3) અને zinc (7.14 g/cm3) થી બને છે. Volume ઉમેરીને તેની density નો અંદાજ કાઢો, માપેલા 8.53 g/cm3 સાથે સરખાવો અને અંદાજ ઓછો કેમ આવે તે કહો.

q.en: A foundry needs 250 kg of sound 70/30 brass castings. Melting loss is 3 % of the charge. Copper costs Rs 820 per kg and zinc Rs 280 per kg. Find the charge mass and the metal cost of the heat.
q.gu: એક ફાઉન્ડ્રીને 250 kg સાચા 70/30 brass castings જોઈએ. Melting loss charge ના 3 % છે. Copper Rs 820 પ્રતિ kg અને zinc Rs 280 પ્રતિ kg. Charge નું દળ અને heat નો metal ખર્ચ શોધો.

q.en: A grey iron contains 3.4 % C, 2.1 % Si and 0.3 % P; a ductile iron contains 3.6 % C, 2.4 % Si and 0.05 % P. Find the carbon equivalent of each and say what it means for casting.
q.gu: એક grey iron માં 3.4 % C, 2.1 % Si અને 0.3 % P છે; એક ductile iron માં 3.6 % C, 2.4 % Si અને 0.05 % P છે. દરેકનું carbon equivalent શોધો અને casting માટે તેનો અર્થ કહો.

q.en: A bracket has a volume of 260 cm3 and is made of steel of density 7.85 g/cm3. Find its mass, the mass if it is made of aluminium alloy of density 2.70 g/cm3, and the percentage saved. The steel has UTS 450 MPa and the aluminium alloy 310 MPa - comment on whether the swap is safe at the same dimensions.
q.gu: એક bracket નું volume 260 cm3 છે અને તે 7.85 g/cm3 density ના સ્ટીલનું બનેલું છે. તેનું દળ, 2.70 g/cm3 density ના aluminium alloy નું બન્યું હોય તો દળ, અને થતી ટકાવારી બચત શોધો. સ્ટીલનું UTS 450 MPa અને aluminium alloy નું 310 MPa છે - સરખા માપ પર આ બદલી સલામત છે કે નહીં તે કહો.

q.en: A 30 m run of 2.5 mm2 wire is to carry 16 A. Compare the resistance and the power lost if the wire is copper (1.72e-8 ohm m) and if it is brass (6.4e-8 ohm m), and say which one a switchboard uses.
q.gu: 2.5 mm2 ની 30 m લાંબી wire 16 A વહન કરે છે. Wire copper (1.72e-8 ohm m) હોય અને brass (6.4e-8 ohm m) હોય તો resistance અને ગુમાવાતી power સરખાવો, અને switchboard કઈ વાપરે તે કહો.

q.en: A 70/30 brass and a gunmetal of composition Cu 88, Sn 10, Zn 2 are given by weight. Convert both to atomic per cent (Cu 63.55, Zn 65.38, Sn 118.71) and say why a metallurgist prefers the atomic figure.
q.gu: 70/30 brass અને Cu 88, Sn 10, Zn 2 ના gunmetal વજન પ્રમાણે આપેલા છે. બંનેને atomic ટકામાં ફેરવો (Cu 63.55, Zn 65.38, Sn 118.71) અને metallurgist atomic આંકડો કેમ પસંદ કરે તે કહો.

learning_outcomes.en: Understand classification, properties and applications of various metallic materials.
learning_outcomes.gu: વિવિધ ધાતુઈ સામગ્રીનું વર્ગીકરણ, ગુણધર્મો અને ઉપયોગ સમજવા.
